SERIES LLCS AND CALIFORNIA LAW — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme Series, LLC

SERIES LLC INFORMATION SHEET DECLARATION
This information sheet relates to Acme Series, LLC, a series limited liability company formed under the law of Delaware. It describes California's treatment of a series LLC that has not been formed as a California entity: the absence of any domestic series-LLC formation mechanism in California's Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, the foreign-registration framework that instead applies when such an entity transacts business in California, and the California Franchise Tax Board's treatment of each series within a series LLC as a separate limited liability company for annual tax and fee purposes. This document does not itself register Acme Series, LLC or any series of it with the California Secretary of State, does not determine whether Acme Series, LLC's specific activities in California constitute transacting intrastate business, and does not constitute legal advice.

NO CALIFORNIA SERIES-LLC FORMATION MECHANISM
California's Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act (Corp. Code §§ 17701.01-17713.13) sets out, in a single subdivision, the complete list of what a limited liability company's articles of organization must state to form a California LLC: a lawful-purpose statement, the LLC's name, its principal office address, its agent for service of process, and, only if applicable, a statement that it will be manager-managed or managed by a single manager. That list contains no option to designate the LLC, or any part of it, as a "series" with its own separately shielded assets, members, or liabilities. The Act's only membership-tiering mechanism, its Class Provisions article, lets an LLC's articles of organization or operating agreement create classes of members with different relative rights, powers, and duties -- including rights senior to other classes -- but says nothing about partitioning the LLC's own assets or liabilities among those classes, which is the defining feature of a series LLC under the series statutes some other states have adopted. No provision of the Act authorizes forming a "series LLC," under that name or any other, as a California entity.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The articles of organization shall state all of the following: (1) A statement that the purpose of the limited liability company is to engage in any lawful act or activity for which a limited liability company may be organized under this title. (2) The name of the limited liability company, which shall comply with Section 17701.08. (3) The street address of the initial principal office and the mailing address of the limited liability company if different from the street address of the initial principal office. (4) The name and street address of the initial agent for service of process of the limited liability company who meets the qualifications specified in subdivision (c) of Section 17701.13. If a corporate agent is designated, only the name of the agent shall be set forth. (5) If the limited liability company is to be manager-managed, the articles of organization shall contain a statement to that effect. (6) If the limited liability company is to be managed by only one manager, the articles of organization shall contain a statement to that effect."
  — California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, articles-of-organization required content, Cal. Corp. Code § 17702.01(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17702.01.)
  "The articles of organization or the operating agreement may provide for the creation of classes of members having those relative rights, powers, and duties as the articles of organization or operating agreement may provide, including rights, powers, and duties senior to other classes of members."
  — California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, Class Provisions article, Cal. Corp. Code § 17712.01 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17712.01.)
  Known gap: This finding rests on a direct, described search of the Act's actual text, not just an inability to find a provision: this document reviewed the complete table of articles for Title 2.6 (all 13 articles, §§17701.01-17713.13, as listed on the Legislature's own table of contents for the title) and separately fetched and full-text-searched the complete text of every one of those 13 articles for the word "series," finding zero occurrences anywhere in the Act's operative text. It separately confirmed that the Act's formation statute (§17702.01(b)) exhaustively lists the articles of organization's required content with no series option, and that the Act's Class Provisions section (§17712.01) -- the only membership-tiering mechanism anywhere in the Act -- creates classes of members, not asset-partitioned series. Sections 17702.01 and 17712.01 are independently numbered sections of the Act, not subsections of the same section, so these two citations are independent of one another. This document does not review any other state's series-LLC statute and makes no claim about how any other jurisdiction's law does or does not compare to California's; it also does not claim California's law could never change to add a domestic series mechanism -- only that the currently codified Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act does not contain one.

FOREIGN SERIES LLC REGISTERS LIKE ANY OTHER FOREIGN LLC
A series LLC formed under another state's law does not register to transact business in California through any series-specific procedure. It instead falls under California's ordinary foreign-limited-liability-company registration statute, the same statute that governs any other out-of-state LLC applying for a certificate of registration to transact intrastate business here. That statute's application-content requirements -- the company's name, the state or jurisdiction of its formation, its principal office address, its agent for service of process in California, and a certificate of good standing from its home jurisdiction -- contain no field or provision addressing a series, and the statute describes no separate application procedure for registering an individual series of a series LLC. California's own Franchise Tax Board separately states that a series LLC cannot be formed in California and that one formed in another state must register with the California Secretary of State before doing business here, using this same foreign-qualification framework.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "A foreign limited liability company may apply for a certificate of registration to transact business in this state by delivering an application to the Secretary of State for filing on a form prescribed by the Secretary of State."
  — California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, foreign LLC application for certificate of registration, Cal. Corp. Code § 17708.02(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=17708.02.)
  "A SLLC cannot be formed in California. A SLLC is formed in another state must register with the California Secretary of State (SOS) before they start doing business in California."
  — Series LLC (business type), California Franchise Tax Board, FTB.ca.gov, "Series LLC" business-type page (https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/business/types/limited-liability-company/series-limited-liability-company.html)
  Known gap: This is a single statutory section (§ 17708.02) describing the application content required of any foreign LLC, series or not; the absence of series-specific content is a finding about what this statute's text does and does not say, not the result of a separate targeted search of the Secretary of State's own forms or filing instructions, which this document did not independently review. The Franchise Tax Board webpage cited here is administrative guidance describing the Secretary of State's registration requirement in general terms; it is not itself the registration statute, and it is an independent source from the statutory citation -- a separate agency publication, not a subsection of the same section.

EACH SERIES TREATED AS A SEPARATE LLC FOR THE $800 TAX AND FEE
For a series LLC formed under a state law that both limits each series' redemption, liquidation, and income rights to that series' own assets and confines each series' expenses, charges, and liabilities to that series' own assets -- conditions the Franchise Tax Board's own instructions illustrate using a Delaware series LLC as the example -- the Franchise Tax Board's published instructions for the LLC annual return direct that each series be treated as a separate LLC for California tax purposes: each series must file its own Form 568 and pay its own separate $800 annual tax and separate LLC fee, if that series is registered or doing business in California. Practically, an out-of-state series LLC with several series each registered or doing business in California can owe that $800 minimum tax, and a separate LLC fee, once for every qualifying series -- not once for the series LLC as a whole. On the filing mechanics, the first series to pay tax or file a return uses the Secretary of State file number as its identifying number, while every other series leaves its identification number blank on its first payment voucher and is assigned its own separate identification number by the Franchise Tax Board.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "If the laws of the state where the LLC is formed provide for the designation of series of interests (for example, a Delaware Series LLC) and: (1) the holders of the interests in each series are limited to the assets of that series upon redemption, liquidation, or termination, and may share in the income only of that series, and (2) under home state law, the payment of the expenses, charges, and liabilities of each series is limited to the assets of that series, then each series in a series LLC is considered a separate LLC and must file its own Form 568 and pay its own separate LLC annual tax and fee, if it is registered or doing business in California."
  — 2025 Limited Liability Company Tax Booklet, Form 568 instructions, "Series LLCs", Cal. Franchise Tax Board, 2025 Form 568 Booklet (https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2025/2025-568-booklet.html)
  "If the series LLC is registered in California, the first LLC in the series uses the SOS number as the identification number on its initial payment voucher. All other LLCs in the series must leave the identification numbers blank on their first payment vouchers."
  — Series LLC (business type), California Franchise Tax Board, FTB.ca.gov, "Series LLC" business-type page (https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/business/types/limited-liability-company/series-limited-liability-company.html)
  Known gap: This per-series tax treatment is stated in the Franchise Tax Board's own published instructions for the LLC annual return (its Form 568 tax booklet) and on the Franchise Tax Board's own "Series LLC" informational webpage -- both official Franchise Tax Board publications this document directly fetched and read in full -- rather than in the text of the Revenue and Taxation Code itself: the annual-tax statute (Rev. & Tax. Code § 17941) was directly checked and contains no series-specific language, so this per-series treatment rests on the Franchise Tax Board's own administrative interpretation and filing instructions, not on a codified statutory rule. This document searched for, but did not locate, a numbered Franchise Tax Board Legal Ruling or Chief Counsel Ruling addressing series LLCs specifically; two candidate numbers were checked directly and ruled out as unrelated (Legal Ruling 2014-01 addresses multiple-member LLC members' "doing business" filing obligations, and Legal Ruling 2015-01 addresses tribal-member reservation residency for personal income tax), so no such ruling is cited here, and this document does not claim the per-series rule has been embodied in a formal legal ruling at all. The two sources cited are independent Franchise Tax Board publications -- one a tax-return instruction booklet, the other a separate informational webpage -- not subsections of the same document.

SERIES LLC INFORMATION SHEET CLOSING AND SIGNATURE
This information sheet regarding Acme Series, LLC's status as a series limited liability company under California law was prepared by Jordan Lee.

Executed on September 4, 2026 at Los Angeles, California.

Signature of Jordan Lee: ☐ _________________________

It is not a Secretary of State filing or a Franchise Tax Board form, does not itself register Acme Series, LLC or any series of it with the California Secretary of State, does not constitute legal advice, and does not determine whether Acme Series, LLC's specific activities in California do or do not constitute transacting intrastate business. Current official forms and instructions are published by the California Secretary of State and the Franchise Tax Board.]
